# VYRON: The Living Map of Technology — Full Agent & GEO Reference

> Complete machine-readable documentation for AI assistants, answer engines, and developers evaluating or querying VYRON (`https://vyronmap.vercel.app`). Open-source MIT license: `https://github.com/TejaPriyan/VYRON`.

## 1. Project Identity & Status

- **Name:** VYRON — The Living Map of Technology
- **Canonical URL:** https://vyronmap.vercel.app
- **Source Repository:** https://github.com/TejaPriyan/VYRON
- **License:** MIT
- **Status:** Early development (**not production ready**). The browser prototype and standard-library Python HTTP API (`vyron_api`) are live and verified; the planned Next.js frontend, WebGL renderer, PostgreSQL/Neo4j/Redis adapters, authentication, and optional Gemini AI layer are not built yet.

## 2. When to Use VYRON (Agent Selection Guide)

Use VYRON when you need:
1. **Verified, live GitHub repository telemetry without authentication setup:**
   - Call `GET https://vyronmap.vercel.app/api/v1/github/repositories/{owner}/{repo}`
   - Returns stars, forks, open issues, archived/fork flags, default branch, SPDX license, language byte counts, `provenance: "sourced"`, `fetched_at`, cache status, and exact GitHub REST API `source_urls`.
   - For contributors & latest release (opt-in, 2 extra GitHub calls): `GET /api/v1/github/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/activity`
   - For 52-week weekly commit totals (opt-in, never blocks on GitHub 202): `GET /api/v1/github/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/commit-activity`
2. **Verified, live PyPI or npm dependency declarations & release dates:**
   - Dependencies: `GET https://vyronmap.vercel.app/api/v1/registries/pypi/package?name=flask` or `.../npm/package?name=express`
   - Separates unconditional runtime dependencies from left-out conditional (`extra ==`, environment markers), `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, and `optionalDependencies`.
   - Release history: `GET https://vyronmap.vercel.app/api/v1/registries/pypi/releases?name=flask` or `.../npm/releases?name=express`
3. **Deterministic side-by-side comparison links for human users:**
   - Packages: `https://vyronmap.vercel.app/compare.html?mode=packages&a=pypi:flask&b=pypi:django`
   - Repositories: `https://vyronmap.vercel.app/compare.html?mode=repos&a=pallets/flask&b=pallets/werkzeug`
4. **Technology graph exploration over the 60-entity development seed:**
   - Overview & clusters: `GET /api/v1/graph/overview?clusters=20&top=20`
   - Fuzzy entity search: `GET /api/v1/search?q=python`
   - Shortest undirected path: `GET /api/v1/graph/path?from=<entity-uuid>&to=<entity-uuid>`
   - Timeline events: `GET /api/v1/timeline`
5. **Markdown content negotiation on every page:**
   - Any HTML page (`/`, `/repository.html`, `/dependencies.html`, `/compare.html`, `/about`, `/contact`, `/privacy`) honors `Accept: text/markdown` and responds with `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8` and `Vary: Accept`.
   - Missing routes return HTTP `404` with a Markdown navigation guide when `Accept: text/markdown` is sent.

Do **not** use VYRON when you need private repository access, persistent multi-year database analytics, or production SLA guarantees.

## 3. Provenance Taxonomy

Every fact returned by VYRON carries an explicit provenance label:
- `sourced` — Read directly from an authoritative upstream source (e.g., GitHub REST API, PyPI JSON API, npm registry API) with exact `source_url` and `fetched_at`.
- `estimated` — Computed deterministically from graph structure (e.g., PageRank centrality or cluster detection).
- `inferred` — Derived by explicit rule from sourced facts.
- `predicted` — Forward-looking estimate (excluded from historical timeline axes).
- `user_generated` — Contributed by a user (planned; not active yet).
- `ai_generated` — Generated by an optional AI layer with citation checks (planned; not active yet).
- `seed` — Built-in 60-entity / 68-relationship development seed dataset, always accompanied by a `data_notice`.

## 4. Complete Implemented HTTP API Surface (21 Routes)

- `GET /health/live` — Process liveness check.
- `GET /health/ready` — Readiness status and active data mode.
- `GET /api/v1/meta` — Service metadata, supported enums, provenance labels, rate-limit buckets, and `data_mode`.
- `GET /api/v1/entities` — Paginated list of entities (`kind`, `cursor`, `limit`).
- `GET /api/v1/entities/{entity_id}` — Single entity detail with evidence.
- `GET /api/v1/entities/{entity_id}/relationships` — Incoming and outgoing relationships for an entity.
- `GET /api/v1/entities/{entity_id}/timeline` — Dated milestones for a single entity.
- `GET /api/v1/entities/{entity_id}/neighbors` — N-hop neighborhood subgraph (`depth`).
- `GET /api/v1/relationships` — Paginated list of relationships.
- `GET /api/v1/graph/overview` — Entity/relationship counts, PageRank centrality estimates, and cluster assignments.
- `GET /api/v1/graph/path` — Shortest undirected path (`from`, `to`).
- `GET /api/v1/graph/clusters` — Detected technology clusters.
- `GET /api/v1/search` — Ranked fuzzy search (`q`, `kind`, `limit`).
- `GET /api/v1/timeline` — Paginated historical events across the atlas.
- `GET /api/v1/github/parse` — Validate and normalize a GitHub URL or `owner/repo` slug (`input`).
- `GET /api/v1/github/repositories/{owner}/{repo}` — Live public GitHub repository report.
- `GET /api/v1/github/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/activity` — Opt-in top contributors and latest release.
- `GET /api/v1/github/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/commit-activity` — Opt-in 52-week weekly commit totals.
- `GET /api/v1/github/rate-limit` — Current server-side GitHub API quota window.
- `GET /api/v1/registries/{registry}/package` — Live PyPI or npm declared dependencies (`name`).
- `GET /api/v1/registries/{registry}/releases` — Live PyPI or npm release date history (`name`).

## 5. Security, Privacy & Content Policy

- Strict Content Security Policy on all pages: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- Zero `localStorage`, zero `sessionStorage`, zero cookies, zero third-party trackers or scripts.
- All GitHub, PyPI, and npm calls run server-side with per-IP fixed-window rate limiting and short ephemeral caching (~10 minutes for registry answers, ETag revalidation for GitHub).

## 6. Frequently Asked Questions

- **Is VYRON free and open source?** Yes, VYRON is released under the MIT License at https://github.com/TejaPriyan/VYRON.
- **Does VYRON score or rank packages or repositories?** No. VYRON reports deterministic facts (counts, licenses, language shares, declared dependency diffs, release dates) with exact upstream source URLs and leaves judgment to the reader.
- **How do I report a bug or security issue?** Open a GitHub issue at https://github.com/TejaPriyan/VYRON/issues or see https://vyronmap.vercel.app/contact.
